blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Executive presence on a call is a learned discipline, not a personality trait. It shows in small signals: the speed at which someone speaks in contested moments, the length of the pause before they answer a hostile question, the choice to wait ten more seconds before typing an immediate response in the chat.

At the most senior level, calls tend to be shorter, sharper and more consequential than regular meetings. A single well-placed sentence can shift a quarter's priorities; a single careless phrase can take weeks to recover from. Experienced executives prepare for difficult calls in advance — not the content, which they already know, but the stance: where they will hold ground, where they will genuinely concede, and what they want the others to walk away thinking about.

Language carries unusual weight in this register. Passive constructions, conditional forms and diplomatic hedging are used surgically, not defensively. "That would be a difficult position to defend at board level" communicates the same message as "I disagree", but leaves the other person with an exit and the speaker with their credibility intact.

items.q: According to the text, executive presence on a call is…
options: a matter of holding the most senior title
a learned discipline rather than an inborn trait
the ability to speak louder than others
a natural gift some people are born with
items.why: "a learned discipline, not a personality trait" — presença executiva se aprende.

items.q: What do experienced executives prepare in advance for a difficult call?
options: The content, which they still need to research
A list of people to blame if it goes wrong
The stance — where to hold ground and where to concede
A longer agenda to control the time
items.why: "not the content, which they already know, but the stance".

items.q: The hedged line "That would be a difficult position to defend at board level" is offered as an example of language that…
options: delivers disagreement while leaving the other person an exit
avoids taking any position at all
hides the speaker's real opinion out of fear
is weaker than a blunt statement
items.why: O texto diz que comunica "I disagree" mas deixa uma saída ao outro e preserva a credibilidade de quem fala.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Wording choices carry real consequences at senior level.
Hedging can be a precise tool, not just evasion.
Speaking faster under pressure projects strength.
A short pause before answering can be deliberate.
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata a velocidade em momentos contestados como sinal a controlar — falar rápido não é a força que o distrator sugere.

items.q: The contrast between "surgically, not defensively" suggests that, for the author, hedging and passive forms…
options: are used precisely and by intent, not to hide
are signs of weakness to be avoided
items.why: Inferência: "surgically" implica uso preciso e intencional; "not defensively" nega que seja para se esconder.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily antes de entrar numa ligação tensa entre dois países. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, give me thirty seconds before we dial in. I've read both sides, and I already know where this call is going to get loud — the pricing floor. So let me be clear with you before we start: that is the one thing I will not move on today. Everything else is genuinely open.

Here's how I want to run it. When São Paulo pushes hard — and they will, in the first two minutes — I'm not going to answer straight away. I'll let the question sit. If I come back fast, it reads as defensive, and we lose the room. A short pause does more work than a clever sentence.

On the margin split, I can give ground. That's a real concession, and I want them to feel it as one, not as something I hand over cheaply. But on the floor, I'll stay calm and I'll stay slow. I'm not going to raise my voice or repeat myself louder. I'll just hold it.

And whatever gets said in the heat of it, nobody types a reply in the chat until I've nodded. Ten seconds of silence beats a message we spend the next fortnight walking back.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is the one thing Emily will NOT move on during the call?
items.why: "the pricing floor… that is the one thing I will not move on today."

items.q: Why won't Emily answer São Paulo straight away when they push hard?
options: Because she needs time to check the figures
Because a fast reply reads as defensive and loses the room
Because the line is usually delayed
Because she wants someone else to respond first
items.why: "If I come back fast, it reads as defensive, and we lose the room."

items.q: On the margin split, Emily plans to…
options: trade it only for the pricing floor
give ground as a genuine concession they should feel
items.why: "On the margin split, I can give ground. That's a real concession… not as something I hand over cheaply."

items.q: Why does Emily insist that nobody type a reply in the chat until she nods?
options: Because the chat is being recorded for legal reasons
Because she wants to read every message herself first
Because a hasty message could take weeks to walk back
Because the chat distracts the other side
items.why: Inferência: "Ten seconds of silence beats a message we spend the next fortnight walking back" — uma mensagem apressada custa caro depois.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's approach to the contested moment?
options: Passive and willing to give up whatever is challenged
Improvised, with no decision made in advance
Aggressive and determined to win every point
Composed and deliberately slow, holding one line while conceding elsewhere
items.why: Inferência: ela pré-decide o inegociável, cede no resto e mantém a serenidade — "I'll stay calm and I'll stay slow."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She kept her composure even as the two teams talked over each other." Composure means…
options: the authority to end the call
a written summary of the meeting
the ability to speak several languages
items.why: Composure = serenidade, autocontrole diante da pressão.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "On the pricing floor she refused to budge; she was determined to ___ throughout the call."
items.why: To hold ground = sustentar a posição, não recuar.

items.q: "He was ready to concede on delivery dates to protect the headline price." To concede means to…
options: yield or give way on a point
items.why: To concede = ceder, abrir mão de um ponto.

items.q: "Her opening line was calibrated to sound firm without sounding hostile." Calibrated here means…
options: carefully adjusted for the intended effect
items.why: Calibrated = calibrado, ajustado com precisão para o efeito desejado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Rather than say 'no' outright, she used ___ — 'that might be hard to defend upstairs' — to soften the refusal."
items.why: Diplomatic hedging = atenuação diplomática, suavizar a recusa deixando margem.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em ligações executivas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "São Paulo pushed back on the pricing floor within the first two minutes." To push back on means to…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We spent a fortnight walking back a comment made in the heat of the call." To walk something back means to…
options: translate it for the other side
retract or soften a statement already made
items.why: Walk back = voltar atrás, retratar ou suavizar algo já dito.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the revised margin split." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "She agreed the concession but expected the other side to follow through on the timeline." To follow through means to…
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Raising your voice won't move the needle in a contested call." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
